title: The cart that cannot hold anything
scenario: A shopping cart class should collect item names. The very first add crashes with the stack trace below.
symptom:
Adding...
Exception in thread "main" java.lang.NullPointerException
	at Cart.add(Main.java:8)
	at Main.main(Main.java:20)
question: What's the root cause?
options: cart is null because new Cart() failed silently
The items field is declared but never assigned a list
List.add rejects the string "milk"
size() is called before add() finishes
explanation: Object fields that are never assigned start as null. The field items is declared on line 5 but no ArrayList is ever created, so items.add(item) on line 8 calls a method on null. The top frame (Cart.add, line 8) is where it blew up; the bottom frame (Main.main, line 20) is how we got there.
fixNote: Initialise the field: items = new ArrayList<>().
debugTip: Read the trace top-down: the first frame, Cart.add at Main.java:8, is the throwing line. Put a breakpoint there, run in debug, and inspect this in the variables view: items shows null, so look for where it should have been assigned.

title: Looking up an unknown user
scenario: The program looks up a user's email and prints it in capitals. For "bob" it crashes instead of printing anything.
symptom:
Exception in thread "main" java.lang.NullPointerException
	at Main.main(Main.java:14)
question: Why is e null on line 14?
options: HashMap cannot store email strings with an @ sign
toUpperCase() returns null for lowercase input
The static map is reset each time findEmail runs
Map.get returns null for a key that is not present
explanation: Map.get returns null when the key is missing, and "bob" was never put in the map. findEmail passes that null straight back, and line 14 calls toUpperCase() on it. A method that can return null forces every caller to check before dereferencing.
fixNote: Check e for null before calling a method on it.
debugTip: The only frame is Main.main line 14. Set a breakpoint on line 13, step over the findEmail call, and watch e: it becomes null right there, which points you back to the lookup rather than the print.

title: Counting letters in a name list
scenario: The loop should add up the lengths of all names in the array. It crashes before printing the total.
symptom:
Exception in thread "main" java.lang.NullPointerException
	at Main.main(Main.java:8)
question: What's the root cause?
options: Slot 2 of the array was never filled, so it is null
The for-each loop runs one index past the end
String.length() fails on two-letter names
total overflows after adding the second name
explanation: new String[3] creates three slots that all start as null. Only slots 0 and 1 get values, so on the third iteration n is null and n.length() throws. A for-each loop never goes out of bounds; it faithfully visits the empty slot too.
fixNote: Skip null entries before calling length().
debugTip: Add an exception breakpoint for NullPointerException and run in debug. The debugger stops on line 8; inspect names in the variables view and you will see [ann, bo, null] with n = null.

title: An NPE with no dot in sight
scenario: A stock counter reads quantities from a map. Apples print fine, then the kiwi line crashes even though it calls no method on a variable.
symptom:
apples=5
Exception in thread "main" java.lang.NullPointerException
	at Main.main(Main.java:11)
question: Why does line 11 throw a NullPointerException?
options: stock itself became null after the first get
HashMap only allows two keys before resizing
get returns a null Integer, and unboxing it to int fails
The string "kiwi" is not a valid map key
explanation: The map holds Integer objects. Assigning one to an int makes Java auto-unbox it by calling intValue() behind the scenes. "kiwi" is missing, so get returns null and the hidden intValue() call throws. getOrDefault supplies 0 instead of null.
fixNote: Use getOrDefault("kiwi", 0) so a missing key gives 0, not null.
debugTip: Breakpoint on line 11, then use evaluate expression on stock.get("kiwi"): it shows null. When an NPE line has no visible dot, suspect auto-unboxing of a wrapper type.

title: Summing three scores
scenario: sum() should add up every element of the array. It crashes with the trace below.
symptom:
Summing...
Exception in thread "main" java.lang.ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException: Index 3 out of bounds for length 3
	at Main.sum(Main.java:5)
	at Main.main(Main.java:13)
question: Which line holds the real mistake?
options: Line 13: scores should be passed as a copy
Line 4: the loop condition lets i reach 3
Line 11: the array literal has the wrong size
Line 5: += cannot be used on array elements
explanation: An array of length 3 has indexes 0, 1 and 2. The condition i <= values.length lets i become 3, and values[3] throws. The message "Index 3 out of bounds for length 3" tells you both the bad index and the size, so the fix is i < values.length.
fixNote: Change <= to < in the loop condition.
debugTip: Top frame is Main.sum line 5. Set a conditional breakpoint on line 5 with i == values.length - 1, then step over once more and watch i go to 3 while the loop keeps running.

title: Trimming names to five letters
scenario: shortName should cut names down to at most five characters. "Margaret" works, "Tom" crashes. The trace starts inside the JDK.
symptom:
Marga
Exception in thread "main" java.lang.StringIndexOutOfBoundsException: begin 0, end 5, length 3
	at java.base/java.lang.String.checkBoundsBeginEnd(String.java:4604)
	at java.base/java.lang.String.substring(String.java:2707)
	at Main.shortName(Main.java:3)
	at Main.main(Main.java:8)
question: Which frame should you look at first?
options: String.checkBoundsBeginEnd, because it is the top frame
String.substring, because the JDK has a bug there
Main.main line 8, because it is the oldest call
Main.shortName line 3, the first frame in your code
explanation: The top frames are inside java.base: that is where the JDK detected the problem, not where it was caused. Scan down to the first frame in your own code, Main.shortName line 3. substring(0, 5) needs at least 5 characters and "Tom" has 3, exactly as the message says: end 5, length 3.
fixNote: Cap the end index with Math.min(5, s.length()).
debugTip: Skip frames that start with java.base/ and put your breakpoint on the first Main frame (line 3). Inspect s and s.length() when it stops for "Tom".

title: Ages copied from a spreadsheet
scenario: Ages pasted from a spreadsheet are parsed and incremented. The first works; the second crashes.
symptom:
31
Exception in thread "main" java.lang.NumberFormatException: For input string: " 42"
	at java.base/java.lang.NumberFormatException.forInputString(NumberFormatException.java:67)
	at java.base/java.lang.Integer.parseInt(Integer.java:652)
	at java.base/java.lang.Integer.parseInt(Integer.java:786)
	at Main.parseAge(Main.java:3)
	at Main.main(Main.java:9)
question: Why does " 42" fail to parse?
options: parseInt does not skip whitespace; the leading space is illegal
parseInt only accepts numbers below 40 by default
The second array element is a char, not a String
The + 1 runs before the string is parsed
explanation: Integer.parseInt accepts an optional sign and digits, nothing else. The quotes in the message, " 42", reveal a leading space. Trimming the input first (raw.trim()) removes surrounding whitespace.
fixNote: Parse raw.trim() instead of raw.
debugTip: Read the exception message carefully: the quotes around " 42" show the hidden space. Then find the first Main frame (parseAge line 3) and inspect raw.length() at a breakpoint: it is 3, not 2.

title: A price with a decimal point
scenario: The program multiplies a unit price by a quantity. Expected "Total: 14.0" but it crashes.
symptom:
Exception in thread "main" java.lang.NumberFormatException: For input string: "3.5"
	at java.base/java.lang.NumberFormatException.forInputString(NumberFormatException.java:67)
	at java.base/java.lang.Integer.parseInt(Integer.java:668)
	at java.base/java.lang.Integer.parseInt(Integer.java:786)
	at Main.main(Main.java:5)
question: Which fix is correct?
options: Wrap line 5 in try/catch and use 0 on failure
Use Integer.valueOf(price) instead of parseInt
Store unit as a double and use Double.parseDouble
Cast the string: int unit = (int) price;
explanation: Integer.parseInt only accepts whole numbers, so the "." in "3.5" is rejected. Integer.valueOf uses the same parser and fails the same way, and you cannot cast a String to int. The value really is fractional, so it must be parsed as a double: 3.5 * 4 = 14.0.
fixNote: Parse with Double.parseDouble into a double variable.
debugTip: Use an exception breakpoint on NumberFormatException; when it stops, step out to the first Main frame (line 5) and inspect price to see the decimal point.

title: Averaging an empty week
scenario: average() returns the mean of an int array. It works for a normal week but crashes for a week with no data.
symptom:
6
Exception in thread "main" java.lang.ArithmeticException: / by zero
	at Main.average(Main.java:7)
	at Main.main(Main.java:14)
question: What's the root cause?
options: sum overflows when the array is empty
The for-each loop throws on an empty array
int[] empty = {} is not legal Java syntax
Integer division by xs.length, which is 0
explanation: For an empty array the loop simply does nothing and sum stays 0, then sum / xs.length is 0 / 0 in int arithmetic. Integer division by zero always throws ArithmeticException: / by zero. Guard the empty case before dividing.
fixNote: Return 0 early when the array is empty.
debugTip: Top frame: Main.average line 7; the next frame shows the caller passed empty (line 14). Breakpoint on line 7 and watch xs.length: it is 0 on the second call.

title: Dividing a double by zero
scenario: Same idea as an average with no items, but this time the total is a double. Nothing crashes. What gets printed?
question: What does this print?
options:
avg = NaN
false

avg = Infinity
true

avg = 0.0
false
Nothing: ArithmeticException: / by zero
explanation: Because total is a double, count is widened to 0.0 and floating-point division is used. IEEE 754 floating-point division of a positive number by zero gives Infinity instead of throwing; only integer division throws. Infinity is greater than 1000, so the comparison is true. (0.0 / 0.0 would give NaN.)
fixNote: Guard count == 0 before dividing.
debugTip: No exception means no stack trace, so set a breakpoint on line 5 and watch avg after stepping over: seeing Infinity tells you a divisor was zero. Double.isInfinite(avg) is handy in evaluate expression.

title: A list of Object that is not all strings
scenario: The loop prints each item in capitals. It prints APPLE, then crashes.
symptom:
APPLE
Exception in thread "main" java.lang.ClassCastException: class java.lang.Integer cannot be cast to class java.lang.String (java.lang.Integer and java.lang.String are in module java.base of loader 'bootstrap')
	at Main.main(Main.java:11)
question: What's the root cause?
options: An Integer was put in the list and then cast to String
toUpperCase() cannot handle the word "pear"
ArrayList cannot hold more than one type of object
The cast should be written (string) o in lowercase
explanation: List<Object> accepts anything, so 42 is autoboxed to an Integer and stored. A cast does not convert an object; it only checks its real type at runtime, and an Integer is not a String. The message names both classes. Checking with instanceof (or using a List<String>) avoids the crash.
fixNote: Only treat the item as a String when instanceof says it is one.
debugTip: Breakpoint on line 11 and inspect o on each iteration: the variables view shows its runtime class (Integer on the second pass). The exception message always names the actual class first.

title: How many bytes in 3 GB?
scenario: A disk tool computes the number of bytes in 3 gigabytes (3 x 1024 x 1024 x 1024). No exception is thrown.
question: What does this print?
options: ArithmeticException: integer overflow
explanation: An int holds at most 2147483647. 3 x 1073741824 = 3221225472 does not fit, and Java int arithmetic silently wraps around (modulo 2^32) instead of throwing: 3221225472 - 4294967296 = -1073741824. Casting one operand to long before multiplying does the math in 64 bits.
fixNote: Make total a long and cast gb to long before multiplying.
debugTip: Overflow throws nothing, so step over line 5 and watch total: a negative result from multiplying positives is the giveaway. Math.multiplyExact(gb, bytesPerGb) would throw ArithmeticException instead of wrapping.

title: Is 0.1 + 0.2 equal to 0.3?
scenario: A price check compares a computed sum to an expected value with ==.
question: What does this print?
options:
true
0.3

false
0.3
explanation: 0.1, 0.2 and 0.3 cannot be stored exactly in binary floating point. The rounded 0.1 plus the rounded 0.2 lands on a slightly different double than the rounded 0.3, so == is false, and printing shows 0.30000000000000004. Compare doubles with a tolerance (or use BigDecimal for money).
fixNote: Compare with a small tolerance instead of ==.
debugTip: Put a breakpoint on line 4 and evaluate a and a - 0.3 in the debugger: the tiny non-zero difference shows why == fails.

title: Two players, one scoreboard
scenario: Ann scores twice and Ben once. The game should show Ann: 2 and Ben: 1.
question: What's the root cause?
options: score is static, so all players share one counter
addPoint() is called on the wrong object
The constructor resets score for every new player
a.score reads Ben's value because b was created last
explanation: A static field belongs to the class, not to each object: there is exactly one score for all Players. All three addPoint calls bump the same variable to 3. Java even lets you write a.score for a static field, which hides the sharing. Removing static gives each Player its own score.
fixNote: Remove static so each Player has its own score.
debugTip: Set a breakpoint on line 21 and expand a and b in the variables view: score is not listed under either object, only under the Player class (static), which shows it is shared.

title: The bonus that never arrives
scenario: addBonus should raise the salary by 500, so the program should print 3500.
question: What's the root cause?
options: addBonus is static, so it cannot change variables
Java passes a copy of the int; the method changes only its copy
The parameter name must differ from the caller's variable
println prints the value cached before the call
explanation: Java is always pass-by-value. addBonus receives a copy of 3000 in its own parameter variable, adds 500 to that copy, and the copy disappears when the method returns. Having the same name as the caller's variable does not link them. Return the new value and assign it in the caller.
fixNote: Return the new salary and assign it: salary = addBonus(salary).
debugTip: Step into addBonus on line 8 and watch salary: it becomes 3500 inside the method. Step out and the caller's salary is still 3000, because each frame has its own variable.

title: A book with no title
scenario: The program should print "Dune / 412". The page count is right but the title is missing.
question: Which line is wrong?
options: Line 2: title must be declared private
Line 13: "Dune" is passed in the wrong position
Line 6: title = title assigns the parameter to itself
Line 14: string concatenation turns the title into null
explanation: Inside the constructor, the parameter title shadows the field title. So title = title copies the parameter onto itself and the field keeps its default, null. Line 7 shows the correct pattern: this.pages refers to the field.
fixNote: Use this.title = title to assign the field.
debugTip: Breakpoint on line 7, then inspect this in the variables view: this.title is still null right after line 6 ran, while the local title is "Dune".

title: The crash points at the wrong method
scenario: An account label should print as "Label: KIM". The trace below has three frames, but none of them is where the mistake is.
symptom:
Exception in thread "main" java.lang.NullPointerException: Cannot invoke "String.toUpperCase()" because "this.owner" is null
	at Account.label(Main.java:9)
	at Main.printLabel(Main.java:15)
	at Main.main(Main.java:20)
question: Where is the root cause?
options: Line 9: label() should check for null and return ""
Line 15: printLabel must not call label() inside println
Line 20: acc should be created with new Account()
Line 5: owner = owner never sets the field
explanation: The message says this.owner is null, so ask: who was supposed to set this.owner? The constructor, but owner = owner assigns the parameter to itself because the parameter shadows the field. A stack trace shows where a bad value was used, not where it was (not) created; this.owner = owner fixes it at the source.
fixNote: Assign the field with this.owner = owner.
debugTip: Read top-down: Account.label line 9 threw, and the message names this.owner. Then search for every assignment to owner and set a breakpoint in the constructor; after line 5 runs, this.owner is still null.

title: Counting vowels word by word
scenario: The program reports how many vowels each word has. Two words print, then it crashes in countVowels.
symptom:
java: 2
debug: 2
Exception in thread "main" java.lang.NullPointerException
	at Main.countVowels(Main.java:4)
	at Main.report(Main.java:13)
	at Main.main(Main.java:19)
question: Where did the null come from?
options: Line 17: the words array contains a null element
Line 4: toCharArray() returns null for short words
Line 13: string concatenation replaces word with null
Line 5: indexOf returns null when no vowel is found
explanation: The top frame (countVowels line 4) is where null was used, and each frame below it passes word along unchanged. Following the trace down to main shows the value came from the array literal on line 17, which contains null. Fix the data or check for null at the boundary.
fixNote: Replace the null entry in the array with a real word.
debugTip: Use an exception breakpoint on NullPointerException. When it stops, click each frame in the call stack panel: word is null in countVowels and report, and in main you can see w came from words[2].

title: Greeting the whole team
scenario: Each team member should be greeted in order. Ana is skipped and then the program crashes inside greet().
symptom:
Hello, Raj
Hello, Lee
Exception in thread "main" java.lang.ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException: Index 3 out of bounds for length 3
	at Main.greet(Main.java:3)
	at Main.main(Main.java:9)
question: Which line holds the real mistake?
options: Line 3: greet should check pos against names.length
Line 7: the array needs a fourth element
Line 8: the loop counts from 1 up to 3 inclusive
Line 9: greet should be passed i - 1 only at the end
explanation: greet() line 3 is where the bad index was used, but greet just trusts pos. The next frame down, main line 9, passed i, and line 8 makes i run 1, 2, 3. Java arrays start at 0, which is also why Ana was skipped. Loop from 0 while i < team.length.
fixNote: Loop with i = 0 and i < team.length.
debugTip: The top frame is in greet, but the bad value arrived as a parameter. Click the Main.main frame in the call stack panel and inspect i: it is 3. Then look at the loop header that produced it.
fixedOutput:
Hello, Ana
Hello, Raj
Hello, Lee

title: Thirty days in milliseconds
scenario: daysToMillis returns a long, so it should handle 30 days (2592000000 ms) easily. One day is right; thirty days is negative.
question: Why is the result negative even though the method returns long?
options: println cannot print longs larger than an int
The multiplication is done in int and overflows first
long values are limited to 2147483647 in Java
The 1000 literal is treated as a short
explanation: All operands are int, so Java multiplies in 32-bit int arithmetic and the product 2592000000 wraps to -1702967296. Only after that is the already-wrong int widened to long for the return. Making one early operand a long (24L) makes the whole chain use 64-bit math.
fixNote: Use the long literal 24L so the multiplication happens in long.
debugTip: No exception here, so set a breakpoint on line 3 and use evaluate expression on days * 24 * 60 * 60 * 1000 and days * 24L * 60 * 60 * 1000 side by side. Math.multiplyExact would have thrown at the overflow.

title: Five JDK frames, one bug
scenario: last() should return the final element of a list. The stack trace is long and mostly JDK internals.
symptom:
Exception in thread "main" java.lang.IndexOutOfBoundsException: Index 2 out of bounds for length 2
	at java.base/jdk.internal.util.Preconditions.outOfBounds(Preconditions.java:64)
	at java.base/jdk.internal.util.Preconditions.outOfBoundsCheckIndex(Preconditions.java:70)
	at java.base/jdk.internal.util.Preconditions.checkIndex(Preconditions.java:266)
	at java.base/java.util.Objects.checkIndex(Objects.java:359)
	at java.base/java.util.ArrayList.get(ArrayList.java:427)
	at Main.last(Main.java:6)
	at Main.main(Main.java:13)
question: What's the root cause?
options: ArrayList.get has a bounds-checking bug in the JDK
queue.add("b") replaced "a" instead of appending
The list must be converted to an array before get
Indexes run 0..size-1, so get(size()) is one past the end
explanation: The first five frames are JDK code doing its job: checking the index and throwing. The first frame from your code is Main.last line 6. A list of size 2 has indexes 0 and 1, so the last element is items.get(items.size() - 1).
fixNote: Use items.size() - 1 as the index of the last element.
debugTip: Skip every java.base/ frame and start at the first Main frame (line 6). Breakpoint there and evaluate items.size() to see that it equals the index you are asking for.

title: Playing fetch with every animal
scenario: play() should make dogs fetch and ignore other animals. The dog works; the cat crashes.
symptom:
fetching!
Exception in thread "main" java.lang.ClassCastException: class Cat cannot be cast to class Dog (Cat and Dog are in unnamed module of loader 'app')
	at Main.play(Main.java:15)
	at Main.main(Main.java:21)
question: What's the root cause?
options: A Cat is an Animal but not a Dog, so the downcast fails
Cat must also define a fetch() method to compile
new Cat() returns null because Cat has no constructor
Dog must override every Animal method for the cast
explanation: The parameter type Animal accepts any subclass, but (Dog) a is checked at runtime against the real object. The second call passes a Cat, which is not a Dog, so the cast throws. Use instanceof (here with a pattern variable) to cast only when it is safe.
fixNote: Only cast and call fetch() when a instanceof Dog.
debugTip: Breakpoint on line 15; on the second hit the variables view shows a is a Cat. The next frame, main line 21, shows which call passed it.
